findings.title: Product over the original space does not preserve the normalization-local annihilation conditions
findings.complete_check: S={xy=0} in C^3, U=S, Z={z=0}, s=0,k=1,m=2, alpha=z^*generator. Normalization A disjoint union B. p_A has z=t^2 on A, identity on B; p_B identity on A, z=t^2 on B. Omega_A=A and Omega_B=B are disjoint neighborhoods covering normalization. Each required local pullback is zero. Product T_A x_S T_B has open-and-closed B_identity x_S A_identity = C_z mapped identically; alpha stays nonzero on punctured z-axis in every neighborhood of s.
assumptions_verified: Reduced Stein S, closed analytic Z, open U and base point s
Finite surjective normalization with two lifts
Both p_i finite surjective between allowed Stein spaces
Disjoint open Omega_i around the two lifts
All stipulated input vanishing conditions in H^1 mod 2
Shrinking-neighborhood condition holds for every Omega
Output product remains finite surjective, but pullback not zero
findings.counterevidence: The proposition and main theorem statements are not refuted; the same data do work if product is taken over the normalization. Normal-space Galois-closure paragraph not contradicted.
findings.impact: Invalid explicitly defined core proof construction; not just OCR or an undefined symbol. Major per core-derivation calibration.

repair.statement: Take product of p_i over normalization, then compose with nu.
repair.verification: Finite surjectivity preserved; all factors share a normalization lift; disjoint inverse-image neighborhoods cover and respective pullbacks vanish, so whole class vanishes.
repair.boundary: Full downstream arguments and independent acceptance remain; author adoption not requested or observed.

findings.title: Introductory exact dimension equality omits the body's pure-dimension hypothesis

location.item: Theorem 0.4 and abstract, compared with Section 1.1 and Remark 5.12(ii)

findings.complete_check: S={point} disjoint union C is normal Stein of dimension 1; K={point} nonempty connected compact Stein with an open Stein neighborhood equal to itself. M(K)=C has cohomological dimension 0, while Theorem 0.4 literally asserts 1.
findings.counterevidence: Corollary 5.11 asserts only <=dim(S); Remark 5.12(ii) already states pure dimension and nonemptiness. Both survive.
findings.impact: Localized scope error in introductory restatement; no core body-bound or sums-of-squares damage demonstrated.

repair.statement: Use the pure-dimension n and nonempty K hypotheses already present in Remark 5.12(ii), or the dimension of the normal connected component containing K.
repair.boundary: No new theorem or author adoption claimed.

scope_clarifications.explanation: Factoring W->X_U rather than just W->Y_U provides finite Stein compactification and preserves qfh refinement; detailed consistent reading in report.

unresolved_claims: Entire global proof not independently reconstructed
Limited literature check cannot exclude all errata

independent_acceptance_check.scope: Focused acceptance of F01 and F02 in arXiv:2305.06054v3; no claim of journal-version equivalence.

checks.result: The exact TeX and source image specify products of nu composed with p_i over S. The crossed identity branches form an open-and-closed punctured-axis component retaining alpha in every neighborhood; finite surjectivity and all local vanishing hypotheses hold. Taking the product over the normalization excludes crossed branches and proves the stated local repair. Prop4.2 to4.3 to Thm5.1 Step5 is explicit.

The introductory equality omits purity under definitions permitting disconnected mixed dimensions. S=point disjoint-union C, K=point gives M(K)=C and cd0, not dimension1. The body already supplies the pure-dimension/nonempty conditions, limiting the impact.

independent_acceptance_check.result: Both findings supported with original severity; no scientific change required.
